rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~90% (from ~97% at the NY open), 50bp 0%, hold ~10% (CME FedWatch 3:01 PM CT); ECB Dec ~90%; BoE Dec ~80%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoC Dec ~44%
rows.read: A December Fed hike is still expected, but bets slipped as stocks fell and US consumers said they expect less inflation. The European Central Bank, Bank of England and Bank of Japan are also expected to hike in December. A softer Fed path would narrow the US rate lead that has carried the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: UoM sentiment Nov final 51.5 (in line; Oct 48.0), current conditions 49.4; UK retail sales Oct +0.7% m/m (fcst 0.0%); Canada retail sales Sep +0.8% (fcst 0.7%)
rows.read: A deep slide in US tech stocks is now a worry for growth in its own right, since falling share prices can make households and companies spend less. US consumers stayed gloomy in November. Commodity currencies like the Aussie and kiwi feel growth fears first.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: UoM 1-yr inflation expectations 3.7% (prelim 4.3%, Oct 4.7%), 5-yr 3.3%; Japan core CPI Oct 2.2%; UK CPI Oct 3.6%; euro-area CPI Oct 4.0%
rows.read: US consumers now expect noticeably less inflation over the next year than they did a month ago, which takes a little pressure off the Fed. Inflation is still above target almost everywhere, so most central banks still lean toward hikes. Japan's prices stayed above the Bank of Japan's goal, keeping a December hike there likely.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: US stocks fell for a seventh day as the sell-off in AI companies deepened, with Nvidia down sharply on a report that a regulator is looking at its accounting. Money ran into the yen and US government bonds, and a gauge of market nerves hit its highest since March. The Aussie and kiwi fell, as they usually do when stocks slide.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC report of Nov 10 (out late after Veterans Day): hedge funds for USD, GBP, AUD and gold; against EUR, NZD, CAD and CHF; slightly against JPY; real money disagrees on EUR, GBP and AUD
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds leaning toward the dollar and the pound and against the euro, the kiwi and the Canadian dollar, with bets against the kiwi growing fastest. Big long-term investors take the other side on the euro, pound and Aussie. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: ECB FSR: France debt 119% of GDP, deficit 5.5%; US October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~4.92% (−13bp, Hercules)
rows.read: France's debts, flagged by the European Central Bank as a risk, keep weighing on the euro. US long-term borrowing costs slipped back below 5% as money ran to safety, but record US government borrowing still weighs a little on trust in the dollar.
